newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela not worried by bolivar's strength - Matos.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela not worried by bolivar's strength - Matos.

text.p: Venezuela is not worried by the recent strength of the bolivar, which has gained over two percent against the dollar over the past week on foreign capital inflows, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.

"Studies show that because the May devaluation was so strong, the recent strengthening of the bolivar has not had a negative effect on the economy," Matos told reporters during a telephone conference from Washington.
In late afternoon trade on Tuesday the unit had firmed to 464 per dollar from Monday's 469 bolivar per dollar close.
"Our worry is rather that we want to maintain its stability and eliminate uncertainty," he said. Bolivar stability is "crucial to our central fight, against inflation."

Analysts agree Venezuela faces a trade-off between a strong currency, used as an anchor against inflation, versus a bolivar that depreciates in line with inflation. The latter would prevent over-valuation while also maintaining Venezuela's precarious recovery in non-traditional exports.
"Fortunately, inflation continues to fall, which shows that our policies are working," Matos said.
Matos said he would be meeting with IMF officials to discuss the effects of recent capital inflows on the exchange rate.
"Although this is not hot money but rather long term investment flows," Matos said, "it does create liquidity problems."
However, the impact of the inflows on base money expansion would fall when the Debt Rescue Fund were finally created, Matos said, and when the country made due foreign debt payments.
In the meantime, "we're sterilizing this liquidity bubble that would otherwise threaten our inflation targets," he said.
